definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded a late-stage policy divergence of 0.16, failing the predicted threshold of >=0.2. This suggests that in the specified 20x20 deterministic gridworld, memory-augmented agents do not develop the hypothesized distinct preference trajectories at this scale of interaction, or the variance is too low to be statistically distinguishable from noise.
definition.limitations: The observed divergence is close to the threshold, implying that the effect might be present but subtle. The current parameter set (10k/200k episodes) may be insufficient for path-dependent preferences to stabilize or differentiate fully.
definition.next_step: Refine the experimental protocol to increase environment dimensionality or vary reward sparseness to see if this amplifies the path-dependent divergence.

definition.next_experiment: Proposed revision of the experimental protocol to manipulate reward density in the gridworld environment.
definition.reason: Previous experiments were inconclusive; the divergence signals suggest a potential effect, but it is currently indistinguishable from noise. Continued testing is required to isolate the conditions under which these preferences manifest.
definition.stop_condition: Confirmation of statistically significant policy divergence or repeated failure after high-variance environment testing.
definition.uncertainty: It remains unclear if memory-augmented systems exhibit genuine stable preference formation or merely transient, low-magnitude state-dependent variance that does not scale with episode count.

definition.reason: The previous experiment failed to meet the support threshold; further hypothesis testing is needed to resolve the inconclusive status.
